newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf to invest $10 bln in manufacturing in 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Gulf to invest $10 bln in manufacturing in 4 years.

text.p: Gulf Arab states plan to invest at least $10 billion in manufacturing projects within four years, a Gulf official said on Tuesday.

"Gulf Arab states planned investment stood at around $10 billion until the year 2000," the secretary-general of the Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) Abdul-Rahman al-Jaafari told Reuters.
GOIC is part of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which groups Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.

Jaafari -- speaking on the sidelines of a seminar to examine Gulf industrial projects and ways of financing them -- said the money would be spent on manufacturing projects, mainly in the petrochemical and metal sectors.

"Our estimates are $18 billion but, taking into account the fact that some projects may not get the go-ahead, we see an investment of not less than $10 billion," Jaafari was quoted by the Gulf Daily News as saying.

He said that total investment in the industrial sector in the GCC now stood at $63 billion. The manufacturing sector's contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) had grown to 9.1 percent in 1995 from 4.8 percent in 1978.
Asked how oil-rich GCC states would finance the planned manufacturing projects, Jaafari said "they will be financed through internal sources and local and international banks".
Jaafari told the seminar that 17 new projects in the GCC worth $140 million were available for investment.

On Monday he said eight projects worth $47.7 million in the engineering sector, four requiring investment of $62 million in the metals sector and two petrochemical projects worth $15.3 million would be offered to potential investors at the seminar.
One project in plastics worth $10.4 million and two worth $4 million in the food sector would also be offered, he added.
